# SecMan web-security check

`secman-web-check` is the merged command-line scanner for two selectable approaches:
bounded HTTP/TLS security checks and headless-browser visual exposure checks. Run
either approach independently or run both against the same explicit target set.

Redirect chains are reported hop by hop. Cross-host transitions and blocked downgrade,
invalid, or over-limit redirects receive distinct findings.

> Scan only systems you own or are explicitly authorized to assess. Passive scanning is
> the default. Active requests and access to RFC1918/ULA targets require separate,
> explicit opt-ins.

## Five-minute quickstart

Prerequisites: macOS or Linux, Python 3.12 or newer, and
[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).

```bash
git clone <repository-url> secman_web_check
cd secman_web_check
./scripts/setup.sh
uv run --locked secman-web-check --help
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com \
  --format all \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on none
```

Replace `https://example.com` with an authorized target. The final command performs a
passive HTTP/TLS scan and writes terminal, JSON, SARIF, and self-contained HTML output.
Machine reports are placed below `scan-output/` and contain findings only—never raw
response bodies.

You can also activate the virtual environment and use the installed command directly:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
secman-web-check scan https://example.com
```

## Common examples

Select the scan approach explicitly:

```bash
# HTTP/TLS checks only (the backward-compatible default)
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --scan-mode security

# Browser screenshot plus vision analysis
SECMAN_VISION_API_KEY='REDACTED' \
  uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --scan-mode visual

# Security and visual scans in one local report
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com \
  --scan-mode both --visual-no-ai --format all --fail-on none
```

`--visual-no-ai` performs deterministic screenshot capture without a model call, so it
cannot report visual-content findings. Screenshots are written below
`OUTPUT_DIR/screenshots` unless `--visual-output-dir` is supplied. Full-page captures
are capped at 4000 pixels.

Scan one public target using safe defaults:

```bash
./scripts/scan-single.sh https://example.com -- --format terminal
```

Verify redirect reporting with the public HTTP testing endpoint:

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://httpbin.org/redirect/1 \
  --format json \
  --fail-on none
```

The JSON findings include `WEB-TRANSPORT-REDIRECT` for the observed hop. Redirects to a
different hostname, HTTPS downgrades, and blocked redirects receive additional rule IDs.

Scan the example target list and write every format:

```bash
./scripts/scan-list.sh examples/targets.txt -- \
  --config examples/config.toml \
  --format all \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on medium
```

Run the documented active probe allowlist:

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --active
```

The `--active` flag enables fixed `TRACE`, `OPTIONS`, `.env`, `.git/HEAD`,
`server-status`, and configuration-backup requests. It does not enable crawling,
arbitrary paths, authentication, exploitation, brute force, or fuzzing.

Scan an authorized private target:

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://10.20.30.40 \
  --allow-private-targets
```

This flag permits only RFC1918 IPv4 and IPv6 ULA addresses. Loopback, link-local,
multicast, unspecified, documentation, and other special-purpose ranges remain denied.
It does not imply `--active`.

## Targets

Supply exactly one positional target, one `--targets-file`, or one `--targets-csv`.
Hostnames without a scheme use HTTPS. Plain target files are UTF-8, one URL or hostname
per line; blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored, and normalized
duplicates are removed.

```bash
secman-web-check scan example.com
secman-web-check scan https://example.com/application/health
secman-web-check scan --targets-file examples/targets.txt
secman-web-check scan --targets-csv testdata/targets-aws.csv
```

AWS target CSV files use this exact header and one account/target pair per row:

```csv
awsAccountNumber,target
111122223333,https://example.com/
444455556666,service.example.org
```

Account numbers must contain exactly 12 digits. The account number is retained in JSON
reports and narrows SecMan subject matching before URI or hostname matching. A normalized
target cannot be assigned to two different accounts in the same file.

User information, URL fragments, non-HTTP schemes, and denied network addresses are
rejected. Every DNS answer and redirect is revalidated. Approved connections pin the
resolved IP while retaining the hostname for HTTP `Host`, TLS SNI, and certificate
verification.

## Reports and exit codes

`--format` is repeatable and accepts `terminal`, `json`, `sarif`, `html`, or `all`.
Terminal is the default. JSON uses schema version `1.0`; SARIF uses version `2.1.0`;
HTML is self-contained, script-free, escaped, and protected by a restrictive CSP.

`--fail-on` accepts `info`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, or `none` and defaults
to `high`.

- `0`: scan completed and no finding met the configured threshold.
- `1`: at least one finding met the configured threshold.
- `2`: invalid configuration, a failed/partial target, or an operational adapter error.

See [Report formats](docs/REPORTS.md) for schemas and examples.

## Configuration

Configuration precedence is CLI, `SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_*` environment variables, the
`[scan]` table in a TOML file, then safe defaults. The example config keeps active and
private scanning disabled.

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan --targets-file examples/targets.txt \
  --config examples/config.toml
```

Secrets are never accepted as CLI values or TOML settings. Vision credentials use
`SECMAN_VISION_API_KEY`; optional `SECMAN_VISION_MODEL` and
`SECMAN_VISION_BASE_URL` select the model/provider. See
[Configuration reference](docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

## Optional MariaDB history

MariaDB access occurs only for `db`, `history`, or a scan with `--store-db`.

```bash
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_HOST=db.example.invalid
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_USER=scanner_user
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_PASSWORD='REDACTED'
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_NAME=secman_web_check

uv run --locked secman-web-check db install
uv run --locked secman-web-check db status
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --store-db
uv run --locked secman-web-check history list --limit 20
```

See [MariaDB setup](docs/DATABASE.md) before applying the example grants.

## Optional SecMan upload

Register separate SecMan scanners for independent lifecycle snapshots: source
`WEB_SECURITY` for security results and source `VISUAL` for visual results. Assign the
same authorized subjects where appropriate. A combined run requires both IDs so one
mode can never resolve findings owned by the other.

```bash
export SECMAN_URL=https://secman.example.invalid
export SECMAN_SECURITY_SCANNER_ID=41
export SECMAN_VISUAL_SCANNER_ID=42
export SECMAN_TOKEN='REDACTED'

uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --scan-mode both \
  --format json \
  --push-to-secman
```

Uploads use `/api/integrations/v1`, never fall back to legacy ingestion, and submit each
target as an atomic snapshot. Partial or failed coverage never resolves older findings.
See [SecMan integration](docs/SECMAN.md).

To resolve the SecMan credentials with Proton Pass, copy the reference-only example,
replace its item paths, log in once, and use the wrapper. It always enables direct
SecMan upload:

```bash
cp examples/secman-proton-pass.env .env
${EDITOR:-vi} .env
pass-cli login
./scripts/scan-with-proton-pass.sh \
  --targets-csv testdata/targets-aws.csv \
  --format json \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on none
```

Use `--env-file FILE` (or `SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_PASS_ENV_FILE`) for another reference file.
`SECMAN_PASS_CLI` may name a non-default `pass-cli` executable. Resolved secrets remain
in the child process environment and are never added to the scanner command line.
The ready-to-edit CSV used above is stored at `testdata/targets-aws.csv`.

For production on AWS, store the same variables as a JSON object in Secrets Manager
and use the normal AWS credential chain (instance role, task role, or workload
identity). The wrapper allowlists environment keys and never prints the returned
secret:

```bash
./scripts/scan-with-aws-secrets.py \
  --secret-id prod/secman/web-check -- \
  https://example.com --scan-mode both --format json --fail-on none
```

## Development and verification

The repository intentionally keeps Python source files directly under `src/`; the build
maps that directory to the installed `secman_web_check` package.

```bash
./scripts/verify.sh
```

The verification script checks the lockfile, tests, Ruff lint/formatting, strict mypy,
the source distribution, and the wheel. Unit tests use deterministic transports and
mock adapters; they do not require a live target, MariaDB instance, or SecMan deployment.

## Documentation

- [Checks and severities](docs/CHECKS.md)
- [Configuration reference](docs/CONFIGURATION.md)
- [Safety and authorization](docs/SAFETY.md)
- [Report formats](docs/REPORTS.md)
- [MariaDB setup](docs/DATABASE.md)

## Limitations

- No crawling, discovery, authentication testing, exploitation, brute force, or
  arbitrary fuzzing. Visual mode executes the selected page in isolated headless
  Chromium with outbound destination checks on every request.
- Active findings use strong bounded signatures but may still require human validation.
- HTTPS targets use SSLyze for the documented TLS capabilities; unavailable individual
  capabilities make the target partial instead of silently clean.
- MariaDB and SecMan behavior is covered with isolated tests here; operators must verify
  connectivity, permissions, TLS trust, and retention policy in their own environment.
# SecMan REST integration

SecMan upload is disabled unless `--push-to-secman` is supplied. This is the direct
result-import path; no separate export/import step is required.

1. Register a `WEB_SECURITY` scanner for security results and a `VISUAL` scanner for
   visual results.
2. Assign their service users and bind only authorized asset subjects.
3. Set `SECMAN_URL` to the HTTPS origin plus `SECMAN_SECURITY_SCANNER_ID` and/or
   `SECMAN_VISUAL_SCANNER_ID` for the selected modes.
4. Set `SECMAN_TOKEN`, or set `SECMAN_USERNAME` and `SECMAN_PASSWORD`.
5. Run a local JSON report first, then repeat with `--push-to-secman`.

The client discovers subjects through
`GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects` and submits atomic target snapshots to
`POST /api/integrations/v1/runs`. Matching prefers the normalized URI and falls back to
the canonical hostname. For `--targets-csv`, the 12-digit AWS account number first
narrows the authorized subject list by `cloudAccountId`, preventing a same-hostname
asset in another account from being selected. Missing or ambiguous matches fail safely.
No inventory is created and no legacy endpoint is attempted.

A complete successful target may resolve older absent findings for that scanner/subject.
Partial and failed results set `completeCoverage=false`, so they never resolve older
findings. Stable external IDs and deterministic run keys make a retry idempotent.

TLS verification is mandatory. Authentication failures and response errors are
sanitized; tokens, passwords, cookies, and raw web response bodies are not uploaded.

Security and visual results intentionally use separate scanner registrations. A
combined run submits two atomic snapshots; the merged local report is not uploaded as
a third snapshot. This prevents a security-only run from resolving visual findings, or
the reverse. `SECMAN_SCANNER_ID` remains a compatibility fallback only for a
single-mode run.

## Proton Pass credentials

The wrapper follows SecMan's `scripts/import.sh` pattern: `pass-cli` resolves references
into a child process environment, then the scanner runs with `--push-to-secman`.

```bash
cp examples/secman-proton-pass.env .env
${EDITOR:-vi} .env
pass-cli login
./scripts/scan-with-proton-pass.sh \
  --targets-csv testdata/targets-aws.csv \
  --format json \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on none
```

The reference file must resolve `SECMAN_URL`, the scanner ID(s) required by the chosen
mode, and either
`SECMAN_TOKEN` or the pair `SECMAN_USERNAME` and `SECMAN_PASSWORD`. Do not put resolved
passwords or tokens in the file. Select another file with `--env-file FILE` or
`SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_PASS_ENV_FILE`; select another executable with `SECMAN_PASS_CLI`.

## AWS Secrets Manager credentials

For production, store the required variables in one JSON `SecretString`. Supported
keys are the SecMan URL, scanner IDs, token or username/password, and optional vision
provider settings. Then run:

```bash
./scripts/scan-with-aws-secrets.py --secret-id prod/secman/web-check -- \
  https://example.com --scan-mode both --format json --fail-on none
```

The script relies on the standard AWS CLI credential chain, rejects unknown JSON keys,
does not echo the secret response, and passes resolved values only in the child process
environment.

## AWS target CSV

`--targets-csv` accepts UTF-8 CSV with this exact header:

```csv
awsAccountNumber,target
111122223333,https://example.com/
444455556666,service.example.org
```

Each account number must be exactly 12 digits and each target must pass the normal URL
and network-policy validation. Blank targets, unexpected columns, malformed rows, and
the same normalized target assigned to different accounts are rejected before scanning.
The account is included in the JSON report and in the SecMan subject-selection step.
A ready-to-edit example is available at `testdata/targets-aws.csv`.
# MariaDB history

Persistence is disabled unless the operator invokes a database/history command or uses
`--store-db`. MariaDB is the only supported database backend.

1. Review [the example grants](../db/grants.example.sql) and replace every placeholder.
2. Create the database/user with an administrative account outside this tool.
3. Export the scanner's least-privilege connection variables described in
   [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md).
4. Run `./scripts/install-db.sh`, then `secman-web-check db status`.
5. Add `--store-db` only to scans whose history should be retained.

The schema stores version/checksum metadata, scan runs, explicit targets, normalized
findings, completeness, and sanitized errors. All target-controlled values use DB-API
parameters. A run write is transactional; a failure rolls it back and returns exit code
2 without removing reports already generated on disk.

Use a trusted CA with `SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_SSL_CA` when the database requires TLS. The
scanner never prints or persists the database password.

# SecMan web-security check

`secman-web-check` is the merged command-line scanner for two selectable approaches:
bounded HTTP/TLS security checks and headless-browser visual exposure checks. Run
either approach independently or run both against the same explicit target set.

Redirect chains are reported hop by hop. Cross-host transitions and blocked downgrade,
invalid, or over-limit redirects receive distinct findings.

> Scan only systems you own or are explicitly authorized to assess. Passive scanning is
> the default. Active requests and access to RFC1918/ULA targets require separate,
> explicit opt-ins.

## Five-minute quickstart

Prerequisites: macOS or Linux, Python 3.12 or newer, and
[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).

```bash
git clone <repository-url> secman_web_check
cd secman_web_check
./scripts/setup.sh
uv run --locked secman-web-check --help
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com \
  --format all \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on none
```

Replace `https://example.com` with an authorized target. The final command performs a
passive HTTP/TLS scan and writes terminal, JSON, SARIF, and self-contained HTML output.
Machine reports are placed below `scan-output/` and contain findings only—never raw
response bodies.

You can also activate the virtual environment and use the installed command directly:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
secman-web-check scan https://example.com
```

## Common examples

Select the scan approach explicitly:

```bash
# HTTP/TLS checks only (the backward-compatible default)
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --scan-mode security

# Browser screenshot plus vision analysis
SECMAN_VISION_API_KEY='REDACTED' \
  uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --scan-mode visual

# Security and visual scans in one local report
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com \
  --scan-mode both --visual-no-ai --format all --fail-on none
```

`--visual-no-ai` performs deterministic screenshot capture without a model call, so it
cannot report visual-content findings. Screenshots are written below
`OUTPUT_DIR/screenshots` unless `--visual-output-dir` is supplied. Full-page captures
are capped at 4000 pixels.

Scan one public target using safe defaults:

```bash
./scripts/scan-single.sh https://example.com -- --format terminal
```

Verify redirect reporting with the public HTTP testing endpoint:

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://httpbin.org/redirect/1 \
  --format json \
  --fail-on none
```

The JSON findings include `WEB-TRANSPORT-REDIRECT` for the observed hop. Redirects to a
different hostname, HTTPS downgrades, and blocked redirects receive additional rule IDs.

Scan the example target list and write every format:

```bash
./scripts/scan-list.sh examples/targets.txt -- \
  --config examples/config.toml \
  --format all \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on medium
```

Run the documented active probe allowlist:

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --active
```

The `--active` flag enables fixed `TRACE`, `OPTIONS`, `.env`, `.git/HEAD`,
`server-status`, and configuration-backup requests. It does not enable crawling,
arbitrary paths, authentication, exploitation, brute force, or fuzzing.

Scan an authorized private target:

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://10.20.30.40 \
  --allow-private-targets
```

This flag permits only RFC1918 IPv4 and IPv6 ULA addresses. Loopback, link-local,
multicast, unspecified, documentation, and other special-purpose ranges remain denied.
It does not imply `--active`.

## Targets

Supply exactly one positional target, one `--targets-file`, or one `--targets-csv`.
Hostnames without a scheme use HTTPS. Plain target files are UTF-8, one URL or hostname
per line; blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored, and normalized
duplicates are removed.

```bash
secman-web-check scan example.com
secman-web-check scan https://example.com/application/health
secman-web-check scan --targets-file examples/targets.txt
secman-web-check scan --targets-csv testdata/targets-aws.csv
```

AWS target CSV files use this exact header and one account/target pair per row:

```csv
awsAccountNumber,target
111122223333,https://example.com/
444455556666,service.example.org
```

Account numbers must contain exactly 12 digits. The account number is retained in JSON
reports and narrows SecMan subject matching before URI or hostname matching. A normalized
target cannot be assigned to two different accounts in the same file.

User information, URL fragments, non-HTTP schemes, and denied network addresses are
rejected. Every DNS answer and redirect is revalidated. Approved connections pin the
resolved IP while retaining the hostname for HTTP `Host`, TLS SNI, and certificate
verification.

## Reports and exit codes

`--format` is repeatable and accepts `terminal`, `json`, `sarif`, `html`, or `all`.
Terminal is the default. JSON uses schema version `1.0`; SARIF uses version `2.1.0`;
HTML is self-contained, script-free, escaped, and protected by a restrictive CSP.

`--fail-on` accepts `info`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, or `none` and defaults
to `high`.

- `0`: scan completed and no finding met the configured threshold.
- `1`: at least one finding met the configured threshold.
- `2`: invalid configuration, a failed/partial target, or an operational adapter error.

See [Report formats](docs/REPORTS.md) for schemas and examples.

## Configuration

Configuration precedence is CLI, `SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_*` environment variables, the
`[scan]` table in a TOML file, then safe defaults. The example config keeps active and
private scanning disabled.

```bash
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan --targets-file examples/targets.txt \
  --config examples/config.toml
```

Secrets are never accepted as CLI values or TOML settings. Vision credentials use
`SECMAN_VISION_API_KEY`; optional `SECMAN_VISION_MODEL` and
`SECMAN_VISION_BASE_URL` select the model/provider. See
[Configuration reference](docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

## Optional MariaDB history

MariaDB access occurs only for `db`, `history`, or a scan with `--store-db`.

```bash
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_HOST=db.example.invalid
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_USER=scanner_user
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_PASSWORD='REDACTED'
export SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_NAME=secman_web_check

uv run --locked secman-web-check db install
uv run --locked secman-web-check db status
uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --store-db
uv run --locked secman-web-check history list --limit 20
```

See [MariaDB setup](docs/DATABASE.md) before applying the example grants.

## Optional SecMan upload

Register separate SecMan scanners for independent lifecycle snapshots: source
`WEB_SECURITY` for security results and source `VISUAL` for visual results. Assign the
same authorized subjects where appropriate. A combined run requires both IDs so one
mode can never resolve findings owned by the other.

```bash
export SECMAN_URL=https://secman.example.invalid
export SECMAN_SECURITY_SCANNER_ID=41
export SECMAN_VISUAL_SCANNER_ID=42
export SECMAN_TOKEN='REDACTED'

uv run --locked secman-web-check scan https://example.com --scan-mode both \
  --format json \
  --push-to-secman
```

Uploads use `/api/integrations/v1`, never fall back to legacy ingestion, and submit each
target as an atomic snapshot. Partial or failed coverage never resolves older findings.
See [SecMan integration](docs/SECMAN.md).

To resolve the SecMan credentials with Proton Pass, copy the reference-only example,
replace its item paths, log in once, and use the wrapper. It always enables direct
SecMan upload:

```bash
cp examples/secman-proton-pass.env .env
${EDITOR:-vi} .env
pass-cli login
./scripts/scan-with-proton-pass.sh \
  --targets-csv testdata/targets-aws.csv \
  --format json \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on none
```

Use `--env-file FILE` (or `SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_PASS_ENV_FILE`) for another reference file.
`SECMAN_PASS_CLI` may name a non-default `pass-cli` executable. Resolved secrets remain
in the child process environment and are never added to the scanner command line.
The ready-to-edit CSV used above is stored at `testdata/targets-aws.csv`.

For production on AWS, store the same variables as a JSON object in Secrets Manager
and use the normal AWS credential chain (instance role, task role, or workload
identity). The wrapper allowlists environment keys and never prints the returned
secret:

```bash
./scripts/scan-with-aws-secrets.py \
  --secret-id prod/secman/web-check -- \
  https://example.com --scan-mode both --format json --fail-on none
```

## Development and verification

The repository intentionally keeps Python source files directly under `src/`; the build
maps that directory to the installed `secman_web_check` package.

```bash
./scripts/verify.sh
```

The verification script checks the lockfile, tests, Ruff lint/formatting, strict mypy,
the source distribution, and the wheel. Unit tests use deterministic transports and
mock adapters; they do not require a live target, MariaDB instance, or SecMan deployment.

## Limitations

- No crawling, discovery, authentication testing, exploitation, brute force, or
  arbitrary fuzzing. Visual mode executes the selected page in isolated headless
  Chromium with outbound destination checks on every request.
- Active findings use strong bounded signatures but may still require human validation.
- HTTPS targets use SSLyze for the documented TLS capabilities; unavailable individual
  capabilities make the target partial instead of silently clean.
- MariaDB and SecMan behavior is covered with isolated tests here; operators must verify
  connectivity, permissions, TLS trust, and retention policy in their own environment.
# SecMan REST integration

SecMan upload is disabled unless `--push-to-secman` is supplied. This is the direct
result-import path; no separate export/import step is required.

1. Register a `WEB_SECURITY` scanner for security results and a `VISUAL` scanner for
   visual results.
2. Assign their service users and bind only authorized asset subjects.
3. Set `SECMAN_URL` to the HTTPS origin plus `SECMAN_SECURITY_SCANNER_ID` and/or
   `SECMAN_VISUAL_SCANNER_ID` for the selected modes.
4. Set `SECMAN_TOKEN`, or set `SECMAN_USERNAME` and `SECMAN_PASSWORD`.
5. Run a local JSON report first, then repeat with `--push-to-secman`.

The client discovers subjects through
`GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects` and submits atomic target snapshots to
`POST /api/integrations/v1/runs`. Matching prefers the normalized URI and falls back to
the canonical hostname. For `--targets-csv`, the 12-digit AWS account number first
narrows the authorized subject list by `cloudAccountId`, preventing a same-hostname
asset in another account from being selected. Missing or ambiguous matches fail safely.
No inventory is created and no legacy endpoint is attempted.

A complete successful target may resolve older absent findings for that scanner/subject.
Partial and failed results set `completeCoverage=false`, so they never resolve older
findings. Stable external IDs and deterministic run keys make a retry idempotent.

TLS verification is mandatory. Authentication failures and response errors are
sanitized; tokens, passwords, cookies, and raw web response bodies are not uploaded.

Security and visual results intentionally use separate scanner registrations. A
combined run submits two atomic snapshots; the merged local report is not uploaded as
a third snapshot. This prevents a security-only run from resolving visual findings, or
the reverse. `SECMAN_SCANNER_ID` remains a compatibility fallback only for a
single-mode run.

## Proton Pass credentials

The wrapper follows SecMan's `scripts/import.sh` pattern: `pass-cli` resolves references
into a child process environment, then the scanner runs with `--push-to-secman`.

```bash
cp examples/secman-proton-pass.env .env
${EDITOR:-vi} .env
pass-cli login
./scripts/scan-with-proton-pass.sh \
  --targets-csv testdata/targets-aws.csv \
  --format json \
  --output-dir scan-output \
  --fail-on none
```

The reference file must resolve `SECMAN_URL`, the scanner ID(s) required by the chosen
mode, and either
`SECMAN_TOKEN` or the pair `SECMAN_USERNAME` and `SECMAN_PASSWORD`. Do not put resolved
passwords or tokens in the file. Select another file with `--env-file FILE` or
`SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_PASS_ENV_FILE`; select another executable with `SECMAN_PASS_CLI`.

## AWS Secrets Manager credentials

For production, store the required variables in one JSON `SecretString`. Supported
keys are the SecMan URL, scanner IDs, token or username/password, and optional vision
provider settings. Then run:

```bash
./scripts/scan-with-aws-secrets.py --secret-id prod/secman/web-check -- \
  https://example.com --scan-mode both --format json --fail-on none
```

The script relies on the standard AWS CLI credential chain, rejects unknown JSON keys,
does not echo the secret response, and passes resolved values only in the child process
environment.

## AWS target CSV

`--targets-csv` accepts UTF-8 CSV with this exact header:

```csv
awsAccountNumber,target
111122223333,https://example.com/
444455556666,service.example.org
```

Each account number must be exactly 12 digits and each target must pass the normal URL
and network-policy validation. Blank targets, unexpected columns, malformed rows, and
the same normalized target assigned to different accounts are rejected before scanning.
The account is included in the JSON report and in the SecMan subject-selection step.
A ready-to-edit example is available at `testdata/targets-aws.csv`.
# MariaDB history

Persistence is disabled unless the operator invokes a database/history command or uses
`--store-db`. MariaDB is the only supported database backend.

1. Review [the example grants](../db/grants.example.sql) and replace every placeholder.
2. Create the database/user with an administrative account outside this tool.
3. Export the scanner's least-privilege connection variables described in
   [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md).
4. Run `./scripts/install-db.sh`, then `secman-web-check db status`.
5. Add `--store-db` only to scans whose history should be retained.

The schema stores version/checksum metadata, scan runs, explicit targets, normalized
findings, completeness, and sanitized errors. All target-controlled values use DB-API
parameters. A run write is transactional; a failure rolls it back and returns exit code
2 without removing reports already generated on disk.

Use a trusted CA with `SECMAN_WEB_CHECK_DB_SSL_CA` when the database requires TLS. The
scanner never prints or persists the database password.

    42	    attribute_risks = _source_risks(policy.get("script-src-attr", scripts))

   130	    def install(self) -> None:
   131	        checksum = hashlib.sha256(_MIGRATION.encode()).hexdigest()
   132	        cursor = self.connection.cursor()
   133	        try:
   134	            statements = tuple(
   135	                statement.strip() for statement in _MIGRATION.split(";") if statement.strip()
   136	            )
   137	            cursor.execute(statements[0])
   138	            cursor.execute("SELECT checksum FROM schema_version WHERE version = %s", (1,))
   139	            row = cursor.fetchone()
   140	            if row is not None:
   141	                existing = row[0] if not isinstance(row, dict) else row["checksum"]
   142	                if existing != checksum:
   143	                    raise StorageError("MariaDB migration checksum mismatch")
   144	            else:
   145	                for statement in statements[1:]:
   146	                    cursor.execute(statement)
   147	                cursor.execute(
   148	                    "INSERT INTO schema_version (version, checksum) VALUES (%s, %s)",
   149	                    (1, checksum),
   150	                )
   151	            self.connection.commit()
   152	        except StorageError:
   153	            self.connection.rollback()
   154	            raise
   155	        except Exception as error:
   156	            self.connection.rollback()
   157	            raise StorageError("MariaDB schema installation failed") from error
   158	        finally:
   159	            cursor.close()

   161	    def status(self) -> SchemaStatus:
   162	        cursor = self.connection.cursor()
   163	        try:
   164	            cursor.execute("SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_version")
   165	            row = cursor.fetchone()
   166	            version = (
   167	                None
   168	                if not row
   169	                else (row[0] if not isinstance(row, dict) else next(iter(row.values())))
   170	            )
   171	            return SchemaStatus(version is not None, None if version is None else int(version))
   172	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - missing schema and driver errors mean not installed
   173	            return SchemaStatus(False, None)
   174	        finally:
   175	            cursor.close()

   199	def resolve_allowed(
   200	    target: NormalizedTarget,
   201	    policy: AddressPolicy,
   202	    resolver: Callable[..., object] = socket.getaddrinfo,
   203	) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   204	    """Resolve a target only when every DNS answer is allowed by policy."""
   205	    port = target.port if target.port is not None else (443 if target.scheme == "https" else 80)
   206	    answers = cast(
   207	        list[tuple[object, object, int, str, tuple[str, ...]]],
   208	        resolver(target.host, port, socket.AF_UNSPEC, socket.SOCK_STREAM),
   209	    )
   210	    if not answers:
   211	        raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} did not resolve to an address")
   212	
   213	    addresses: list[str] = []
   214	    for answer in answers:
   215	        value = answer[4][0]
   216	        try:
   217	            address = ipaddress.ip_address(value)
   218	        except ValueError as error:
   219	            raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} resolved to an invalid address") from error
   220	        if not policy.allows(address):
   221	            raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} resolved to a denied address")
   222	        normalized = str(address)
   223	        if normalized not in addresses:
   224	            addresses.append(normalized)
   225	    return tuple(addresses)

   228	def _normalize_host(host: str) -> str:
   229	    try:
   230	        return str(ipaddress.ip_address(host))
   231	    except ValueError:
   232	        pass
   233	    if any(character in host for character in "/\\@"):
   234	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid")
   235	    try:
   236	        normalized = host.encode("idna").decode("ascii").lower()
   237	    except UnicodeError as error:
   238	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid") from error
   239	    if not normalized or any(
   240	        character.isspace() or ord(character) < 32 for character in normalized
   241	    ):
   242	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid")
   243	    return normalized

   199	def resolve_allowed(
   200	    target: NormalizedTarget,
   201	    policy: AddressPolicy,
   202	    resolver: Callable[..., object] = socket.getaddrinfo,
   203	) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   204	    """Resolve a target only when every DNS answer is allowed by policy."""
   205	    port = target.port if target.port is not None else (443 if target.scheme == "https" else 80)
   206	    answers = cast(
   207	        list[tuple[object, object, int, str, tuple[str, ...]]],
   208	        resolver(target.host, port, socket.AF_UNSPEC, socket.SOCK_STREAM),
   209	    )
   210	    if not answers:
   211	        raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} did not resolve to an address")
   212	
   213	    addresses: list[str] = []
   214	    for answer in answers:
   215	        value = answer[4][0]
   216	        try:
   217	            address = ipaddress.ip_address(value)
   218	        except ValueError as error:
   219	            raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} resolved to an invalid address") from error
   220	        if not policy.allows(address):
   221	            raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} resolved to a denied address")
   222	        normalized = str(address)
   223	        if normalized not in addresses:
   224	            addresses.append(normalized)
   225	    return tuple(addresses)

   228	def _normalize_host(host: str) -> str:
   229	    try:
   230	        return str(ipaddress.ip_address(host))

   233	    if any(character in host for character in "/\\@"):
   234	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid")
   235	    try:
   236	        normalized = host.encode("idna").decode("ascii").lower()
   237	    except UnicodeError as error:
   238	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid") from error
   239	    if not normalized or any(
   240	        character.isspace() or ord(character) < 32 for character in normalized
   241	    ):
   242	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid")
   243	    return normalized

   130	    def install(self) -> None:
   131	        checksum = hashlib.sha256(_MIGRATION.encode()).hexdigest()
   132	        cursor = self.connection.cursor()
   133	        try:
   134	            statements = tuple(
   135	                statement.strip() for statement in _MIGRATION.split(";") if statement.strip()
   136	            )
   137	            cursor.execute(statements[0])
   138	            cursor.execute("SELECT checksum FROM schema_version WHERE version = %s", (1,))
   139	            row = cursor.fetchone()
   140	            if row is not None:
   141	                existing = row[0] if not isinstance(row, dict) else row["checksum"]
   142	                if existing != checksum:
   143	                    raise StorageError("MariaDB migration checksum mismatch")
   144	            else:
   145	                for statement in statements[1:]:
   146	                    cursor.execute(statement)
   147	                cursor.execute(
   148	                    "INSERT INTO schema_version (version, checksum) VALUES (%s, %s)",
   149	                    (1, checksum),
   150	                )
   151	            self.connection.commit()
   152	        except StorageError:
   153	            self.connection.rollback()
   154	            raise
   155	        except Exception as error:
   156	            self.connection.rollback()
   157	            raise StorageError("MariaDB schema installation failed") from error
   158	        finally:
   159	            cursor.close()

   161	    def status(self) -> SchemaStatus:
   162	        cursor = self.connection.cursor()
   163	        try:
   164	            cursor.execute("SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_version")
   165	            row = cursor.fetchone()
   166	            version = (
   167	                None
   168	                if not row
   169	                else (row[0] if not isinstance(row, dict) else next(iter(row.values())))
   170	            )
   171	            return SchemaStatus(version is not None, None if version is None else int(version))
   172	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - missing schema and driver errors mean not installed
   173	            return SchemaStatus(False, None)
   174	        finally:
   175	            cursor.close()

   199	def resolve_allowed(
   200	    target: NormalizedTarget,
   201	    policy: AddressPolicy,
   202	    resolver: Callable[..., object] = socket.getaddrinfo,
   203	) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   204	    """Resolve a target only when every DNS answer is allowed by policy."""
   205	    port = target.port if target.port is not None else (443 if target.scheme == "https" else 80)
   206	    answers = cast(
   207	        list[tuple[object, object, int, str, tuple[str, ...]]],
   208	        resolver(target.host, port, socket.AF_UNSPEC, socket.SOCK_STREAM),
   209	    )
   210	    if not answers:
   211	        raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} did not resolve to an address")
   212	
   213	    addresses: list[str] = []
   214	    for answer in answers:
   215	        value = answer[4][0]
   216	        try:
   217	            address = ipaddress.ip_address(value)
   218	        except ValueError as error:
   219	            raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} resolved to an invalid address") from error
   220	        if not policy.allows(address):
   221	            raise AddressDenied(f"target {target.host} resolved to a denied address")
   222	        normalized = str(address)
   223	        if normalized not in addresses:
   224	            addresses.append(normalized)
   225	    return tuple(addresses)

   228	def _normalize_host(host: str) -> str:
   229	    try:
   230	        return str(ipaddress.ip_address(host))
   231	    except ValueError:
   232	        pass
   233	    if any(character in host for character in "/\\@"):
   234	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid")
   235	    try:
   236	        normalized = host.encode("idna").decode("ascii").lower()
   237	    except UnicodeError as error:
   238	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid") from error
   239	    if not normalized or any(
   240	        character.isspace() or ord(character) < 32 for character in normalized
   241	    ):
   242	        raise TargetError("target host is invalid")
   243	    return normalized

   210	def _parse_analysis(
   211	    payload: Mapping[str, Any], target: NormalizedTarget, model: str
   212	) -> list[Finding]:
   213	    choices = payload.get("choices")
   214	    if not isinstance(choices, list) or not choices:
   215	        raise ValueError("vision provider returned no choices")
   216	    message = choices[0].get("message") if isinstance(choices[0], dict) else None
   217	    content = message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else None
   218	    if not isinstance(content, str):
   219	        raise TypeError("vision provider returned no text")
   220	    fenced = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*\})\s*```", content, re.DOTALL)
   221	    document = json.loads(fenced.group(1) if fenced else content)
   222	    rows = document.get("findings", []) if isinstance(document, dict) else []
   223	    if not isinstance(rows, list):
   224	        raise TypeError("vision findings must be a list")
   225	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   226	    for row in rows[:100]:
   227	        if not isinstance(row, dict) or not str(row.get("title", "")).strip():
   228	            continue
   229	        category = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_-]+", "-", str(row.get("category", "other")).lower())
   230	        severity_name = str(row.get("severity", "MEDIUM")).upper()
   231	        severity = Severity.__members__.get(severity_name, Severity.MEDIUM)
   232	        try:
   233	            confidence = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(row.get("confidence", 0.5))))
   234	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
   235	            confidence = 0.5
   236	        findings.append(
   237	            Finding.create(
   238	                f"VISUAL-{category or 'other'}",
   239	                target.url,
   240	                severity,
   241	                str(row["title"])[:300],
   242	                confidence=confidence,
   243	                description="Sensitive content detected by screenshot analysis.",
   244	                recommendation=str(row.get("recommendation", ""))[:2000],
   245	                evidence=str(row.get("evidence", ""))[:2000],
   246	                engine="secman-web-check-visual",
   247	                model=model,
   248	            )
   249	        )
   250	    return findings

   253	async def _analyze(capture: PageCapture, options: VisualOptions) -> list[Finding]:
   254	    if capture.screenshot_path is None or options.api_key is None:
   255	        return []
   256	    encoded = base64.b64encode(capture.screenshot_path.read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
   257	    prompt = (
   258	        f"Requested URL: {capture.requested_url}\nFinal URL: {capture.final_url}\n"
   259	        f"HTTP status: {capture.status_code}\nTitle: {capture.title}\nPage text: {capture.text}"
   260	    )
   261	    body = {
   262	        "model": options.model,
   263	        "temperature": 0,
   264	        "max_tokens": 2000,
   265	        "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
   266	        "messages": [
   267	            {"role": "system", "content": _SYSTEM_PROMPT},
   268	            {
   269	                "role": "user",
   270	                "content": [
   271	                    {"type": "text", "text": prompt},
   272	                    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{encoded}"}},
   273	                ],
   274	            },
   275	        ],
   276	    }
   277	    provider = normalize_target(options.base_url)
   278	    addresses = await asyncio.to_thread(resolve_allowed, provider, AddressPolicy())
   279	
   280	    def post() -> httpx.Response:
   281	        with httpx.Client(
   282	            base_url=options.base_url.rstrip("/"),
   283	            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {options.api_key}"},
   284	            timeout=options.timeout_seconds,
   285	            follow_redirects=False,
   286	            trust_env=False,
   287	            transport=pinned_transport(provider, addresses),
   288	        ) as client:
   289	            return client.post("/chat/completions", json=body)
   290	
   291	    response = await asyncio.to_thread(post)
   292	    try:
   293	        response.raise_for_status()
   294	        payload = response.json()
   295	    finally:
   296	        response.close()
   297	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   298	        raise TypeError("vision provider returned an invalid response")
   299	    return _parse_analysis(payload, normalize_target(capture.requested_url), options.model)

   302	async def _scan_visual_async(
   303	    targets: Sequence[NormalizedTarget], config: ScannerConfig, options: VisualOptions
   304	) -> ScanRun:
   305	    started = datetime.now(UTC)
   306	    results: list[TargetResult | None] = [None] * len(targets)
   307	    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(config.concurrency)
   308	    async with BrowserCapturer(options, config) as capturer:
   309	
   310	        async def process(index: int, target: NormalizedTarget) -> None:
   311	            target_started = datetime.now(UTC)
   312	            async with semaphore:
   313	                capture = await capturer.capture(target, index + 1)
   314	            errors: list[str] = []
   315	            findings: list[Finding] = []
   316	            if capture.error:
   317	                errors.append(capture.error)
   318	            elif options.analyze:
   319	                try:
   320	                    findings = await _analyze(capture, options)
   321	                except (httpx.HTTPError, OSError, TypeError, ValueError):
   322	                    errors.append("visual analysis failed")
   323	            complete = not errors
   324	            results[index] = TargetResult(
   325	                target=target,
   326	                status=TargetStatus.SUCCESS if complete else TargetStatus.PARTIAL,
   327	                findings=tuple(findings),
   328	                errors=tuple(errors),
   329	                complete=complete,
   330	                started_at=target_started,
   331	                completed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
   332	            )
   333	
   334	        await asyncio.gather(*(process(index, target) for index, target in enumerate(targets)))
   335	    return ScanRun(
   336	        run_id=str(uuid4()),
   337	        targets=tuple(result for result in results if result is not None),
   338	        started_at=started,
   339	        completed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
   340	    )
   341	
   342	
   343	def scan_visual_all(
   344	    targets: Sequence[NormalizedTarget], config: ScannerConfig, options: VisualOptions
   345	) -> ScanRun:
   346	    """Capture and optionally analyze all targets while preserving input order."""
   347	    return asyncio.run(_scan_visual_async(targets, config, options))
   348	
   349	
   350	def merge_runs(security: ScanRun, visual: ScanRun) -> ScanRun:
   351	    """Merge same-target results for local reports; uploads retain separate snapshots."""
   352	    visual_by_url = {result.target.url: result for result in visual.targets}
   353	    merged: list[TargetResult] = []
   354	    for left in security.targets:
   355	        right = visual_by_url[left.target.url]
   356	        complete = left.complete and right.complete
   357	        merged.append(
   358	            TargetResult(
   359	                target=left.target,
   360	                status=TargetStatus.SUCCESS if complete else TargetStatus.PARTIAL,
   361	                findings=tuple(
   362	                    {item.external_id: item for item in (*left.findings, *right.findings)}.values()
   363	                ),
   364	                errors=tuple(dict.fromkeys((*left.errors, *right.errors))),
   365	                complete=complete,
   366	                started_at=min(left.started_at, right.started_at),
   367	                completed_at=max(left.completed_at, right.completed_at),
   368	            )
   369	        )
   370	    return ScanRun(
   371	        run_id=str(uuid4()),
   372	        targets=tuple(merged),
   373	        started_at=min(security.started_at, visual.started_at),
   374	        completed_at=max(security.completed_at, visual.completed_at),
   375	    )

content.text:
The existing architecture is a good base: standalone target lists, MariaDB history, SecMan subjects, atomic result submission, asset URIs, and network zones already exist. The clean extension is to add a separate component-inventory and exposure lifecycle—not encode detected software as vulnerabilities or CrowdStrike-installed products.

## 1. Optimized prompt

```text
Act as a senior security architect and implementation planner for SecMan.

Repositories:
- Main: /Users/flake/sources/misc/secman
- Independent extension: extensions/secman_web_check

For this first pass, do not edit code. Inspect the live dev branches, CLAUDE.md,
AGENTS.md, the current integration-result contract, scanner models, target loading,
MariaDB storage, SecMan asset model, MCP permissions, and vulnerability analytics UI.
Then produce an implementation-ready design and phased plan.

Objective

Extend secman_web_check so every web scan can produce a best-effort inventory of
detected software components:

- JavaScript libraries
- CSS libraries/frameworks
- Web servers and reverse-proxy products

Each detected component must include, when known:

- normalized category, product name, vendor, and version
- confidence
- detector/signature identifier and signature-catalog version
- bounded, sanitized evidence type and source URL
- first/last observation timestamps once stored centrally

The inventory must be:

1. printed in terminal output;
2. included in versioned JSON and HTML reports;
3. optionally persisted in the extension's existing MariaDB database;
4. submitted to SecMan alongside an atomic integration run;
5. queryable through SecMan REST and MCP;
6. visible in a Vulnerability Management analytics view showing:
   - configured and observed external exposure;
   - registered, scanned, stale, failed, and unscanned assets;
   - current software components and versions;
   - component-to-asset drilldowns.

Target sources

Preserve the existing positional target, --targets-file, and --targets-csv inputs.
Add a mutually exclusive SecMan-managed source that retrieves every paginated subject
explicitly assigned to the WEB_SECURITY scanner. Preserve the returned subjectId and
assetId so submission does not need fuzzy URI/hostname matching.

A standalone target must remain fully scannable and locally storable without SecMan.
Submitting an unbound standalone target to SecMan must fail safely and identify the
unmatched target; it must not silently create assets or scanner bindings.

Semantics

- Treat component detection as inventory, not as a vulnerability finding.
- Do not store it in integration metadataJson as an opaque blob.
- Do not reuse installed_product: CrowdStrike owns that snapshot lifecycle.
- Keep current WEB_SECURITY findings projected as the generic Webserver product.
- Distinguish configured exposure (Asset.networkZone and URI) from observed
  reachability from a named scanner vantage point.
- “Reachable” means reachable from that scanner deployment, not universally reachable.
- A complete successful component snapshot may resolve absent components.
  Partial, failed, truncated, budget-limited, or policy-denied scans must not.
- Never infer a version unless an explicit bounded signal supports it.
- Never persist or upload raw HTML, JavaScript, CSS, cookies, credentials, or
  unredacted query strings.

Detection boundaries

Use a deterministic, versioned, data-driven signature engine. Analyze response headers,
HTML metadata, script URLs, stylesheet URLs, and bounded transient resource content.
Same-origin referenced JS/CSS may be fetched only within strict per-resource and
per-target budgets using the existing DNS revalidation and pinned-IP transport.
Do not fetch cross-origin resources merely for fingerprinting; their sanitized URL may
be used as a signal. Do not crawl, execute new active probes, use authentication,
download source maps, or weaken TLS/SSRF controls.

Persistence and API

Continue using MariaDB; do not introduce SQLite. Preserve migration 001 and add ordered,
checksum-verified migrations.

Extend the existing /api/integrations/v1 run contract additively with a validated,
optional inventory block. REST is the canonical machine interface. MCP must delegate
to the same service layer and preserve identical asset scoping.

Reuse:
- GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects
- list_integration_subjects
- POST /api/integrations/v1/runs
- submit_integration_run

Add bounded, paginated REST/MCP reads for exposure summary, exposure rows, and web
components. Register every new MCP tool in both McpToolPermissions.LISTING and CALLING
and require delegation plus the narrowest appropriate permission.

The repository contains no SOAP implementation. Treat “SOAP/REST” as a requirement for
a programmatic API and make REST canonical. Describe a separate SOAP-adapter option,
but do not introduce SOAP, WSDL tooling, or a scanner-hosted service unless an actual
legacy consumer, authentication method, and WSDL contract are supplied.

Security and compatibility

Preserve passive defaults, explicit --active and --allow-private-targets opt-ins,
per-hop DNS validation, pinned IP connections with original Host/SNI, TLS verification,
proxy disabling, bounded inputs, parameterized SQL, sanitized errors, asset-level RBAC,
and no legacy cli-add fallback.

Keep scanner runtime and its tests, migrations, scripts, fixtures, and documentation
inside extensions/secman_web_check. Main-repository changes should be limited to the
backend contract/storage/services, MCP, frontend analytics, tests, and central docs.
The repositories are independent and all agent-authored changes belong on dev.

Deliverables

1. Current-state gap analysis with file references.
2. Architecture and data-flow diagram.
3. Scanner domain model and signature-catalog design.
4. Local and SecMan database schemas and lifecycle rules.
5. Exact REST payloads/endpoints and MCP tool contracts.
6. CLI and report-format changes.
7. UI layout and filters.
8. Security/threat analysis.
9. Backward-compatible deployment sequence.
10. Phased implementation plan with files and tests.
11. Explicit acceptance criteria and unresolved decisions.

Definition of done must include extension verify.sh, focused backend/frontend tests,
integration-contract verification, OWASP review, MCP permission parity, and the
repository-mandated E2E gates against an explicitly confirmed disposable environment.
```

## 2. Proposed design

### Grounded starting point

The extension already has:

- Three standalone target inputs in [cli.py](/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman/extensions/secman_web_check/src/cli.py:137).
- Optional MariaDB run/target/finding history in [storage.py](/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman/extensions/secman_web_check/src/storage.py:60).
- SecMan subject discovery and atomic REST submission in [secman.py](/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman/extensions/secman_web_check/src/secman.py:216).
- Existing asset `uri` and `networkZone` fields in [Asset.kt](/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman/src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/domain/Asset.kt:76).
- Atomic finding lifecycle through [IntegrationScanService.kt](/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman/src/backendng/src/main/kotlin/com/secman/service/IntegrationScanService.kt:43).
- A deliberate generic `Webserver` vulnerability product for web-security findings in [V266__web_security_finding_product.sql](/Users/flake/sources/misc/secman/src/backendng/src/main/resources/db/migration/V266__web_security_finding_product.sql:1).

### Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SecMan assigned subjects] --> S[secman_web_check]
    B[Single URL / file / CSV] --> S
    S --> C[Bounded HTTP/TLS collection]
    C --> D[Component fingerprint engine]
    D --> R[Target result: findings + exposure + components]
    R --> T[Terminal / JSON / HTML]
    R --> M[Optional local MariaDB]
    R --> I[SecMan integration REST snapshot]
    I --> X[Current exposure and component lifecycle]
    X --> U[Vulnerability Analytics view]
    X --> P[REST and MCP reads]
```

### Scanner model

Add three concepts:

| Concept | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ScanTargetRef` | Wraps the normalized URL with source, optional `subjectId`, `assetId`, and cloud account. |
| `ExposureObservation` | Requested/effective URL, HTTP status, redirect count, reachability, observation time and vantage label. |
| `DetectedComponent` | Stable key, category, name, vendor/version, confidence, signature ID/catalog version and bounded evidence. |

Initial component categories should remain limited to `JAVASCRIPT_LIBRARY`, `CSS_LIBRARY`, and `WEB_SERVER`.

A component key should be based on category, canonical name, and explicit version—or `unknown`—not evidence text or URL. Duplicate signals then merge, retaining the strongest confidence and a small bounded evidence set.

### Detection engine

Use a versioned in-repository signature catalogue rather than embedding product-specific logic throughout checks.

Signals, strongest first:

1. Exact server/header signatures.
2. Versioned script or stylesheet URLs.
3. HTML `meta generator`, script/link attributes and integrity metadata.
4. Bounded same-origin JS/CSS content signatures.
5. Browser-observed resource URLs when visual mode is already running.

Resource inspection must be bounded—for example, at most 20 same-origin resources, 256 KiB each and 2 MiB total per target. Cross-origin resources should not be fetched for fingerprinting.

Component coverage gets its own `coverageComplete` flag. Hitting a body/resource limit must not make older components disappear.

### Local persistence

Preserve migration `001_initial.sql`. Add an immutable migration 002 and make the installer execute missing migrations by version and checksum.

Add:

1. Exact server/header signatures.
2. Versioned script or stylesheet URLs.
3. HTML `meta generator`, script/link attributes and integrity metadata.
4. Bounded same-origin JS/CSS content signatures.
5. Browser-observed resource URLs when visual mode is already running.

Resource inspection must be bounded—for example, at most 20 same-origin resources, 256 KiB each and 2 MiB total per target. Cross-origin resources should not be fetched for fingerprinting.

Component coverage gets its own `coverageComplete` flag. Hitting a body/resource limit must not make older components disappear.

### Local persistence

Preserve migration `001_initial.sql`. Add an immutable migration 002 and make the installer execute missing migrations by version and checksum.

Add:

- Exposure fields to `scan_target`: effective URL, reachability, HTTP status, component coverage, catalogue version.
- `scan_component`, linked to `scan_target`, with a unique target/component key.
- A `history show RUN_ID` or equivalent command that prints stored exposure and components.

Terminal, JSON and HTML should show a distinct component table. SARIF should remain finding-oriented; inventory rows are not SARIF security results. Use a backwards-compatible JSON schema bump such as `1.1`.

### SecMan contract

Extend `POST /api/integrations/v1/runs` and `submit_integration_run` with an optional block:

```json
{
  "inventory": {
    "schemaVersion": "1.0",
    "catalogVersion": "2026.09",
    "coverageComplete": true,
    "exposure": {
      "requestedUrl": "https://app.example/",
      "effectiveUrl": "https://app.example/login",
      "reachability": "REACHABLE",
      "httpStatus": 200,
      "redirectCount": 1,
      "vantagePoint": "external-eu-1"
    },
    "components": [
      {
        "componentKey": "js-library:jquery:3.7.1",
        "category": "JAVASCRIPT_LIBRARY",
        "name": "jQuery",
        "vendor": "OpenJS Foundation",
        "version": "3.7.1",
        "confidence": 0.98,
        "signatureId": "jquery-script-url",
        "evidenceType": "SCRIPT_URL",
        "sourceUrl": "https://app.example/static/jquery-3.7.1.min.js"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Validate enums, lengths, URL schemes, confidence, duplicate keys and component-count limits before entering the transaction. Only `WEB_SECURITY` scanners should be allowed to submit this inventory.

SecMan storage should add:

- `integration_run.inventory_json` for immutable historical evidence.
- `web_exposure` for the latest observation per subject.
- `web_component` for current component lifecycle, with first seen, last seen, resolved time and last run.

Do not put this in `installed_product`: its clean-state CrowdStrike importer could otherwise delete or overwrite web observations.

### Exposure semantics

Keep these states separate:

- Configured external: asset has HTTP(S) URI and `networkZone` of `EXTERNAL` or `DMZ`.
- Observed reachable: the scanner received an HTTP response from its declared vantage.
- Not reachable from scanner: connection failed from that vantage.
- Unknown: policy denial, scanner failure or insufficient evidence.

An HTTP 404 or 500 is still reachable. A DNS-policy rejection is `UNKNOWN`, not “not reachable.” Scans should never automatically rewrite an operator’s `networkZone`.

### Target sources

Add `--targets-from-secman` as a fourth mutually exclusive input source.

It should:

- Page through every subject assigned to the configured `WEB_SECURITY` scanner.
- Require an HTTP(S) subject URI.
- Retain `subjectId` directly through the scan.
- Submit results without hostname fallback matching.

Existing standalone sources remain unchanged. A standalone target can still be matched to an existing subject for upload, but missing or ambiguous bindings must fail safely. Automatic asset creation/binding should be a later, explicit administrative workflow with dry-run support—not a side effect of scanning.

### REST, MCP and SOAP

Recommended REST reads:

- `GET /api/integrations/v1/web-exposure/summary`
- `GET /api/integrations/v1/web-exposures`
- `GET /api/integrations/v1/web-components`
- `GET /api/integrations/v1/web-components/{key}/assets`

All must be paginated and filtered through accessible asset IDs before aggregation.

MCP should reuse target discovery and submission, then add:

- `get_web_exposure_summary`
- `list_web_exposures`
- `list_web_components`

REST and MCP must call the same services so their RBAC and results cannot drift.

There is no SOAP foundation in the repository. I would not add one now. If a real legacy SOAP consumer exists, implement a thin adapter over the same services, with strict XSD validation, disabled DTD/external entities, bounded documents and established authentication. It should not become a separate business-logic path.

### SecMan analytics UI

Add an `External exposure` tab to the existing Vulnerability Management analytics page, with a standalone deep link such as `/vulnerabilities/external-exposure`.

The view should contain:

- Summary cards: configured external, observed reachable, scanned, stale, failed, unscanned and unique components.
- Exposure table: asset, configured zone, requested/effective URI, observed status, HTTP status, scanner vantage, last observation and component count.
- Components table: category, product, version, reachable asset count, first/last seen and confidence.
- Asset/component drilldowns.
- Filters for owner, workgroup, reachability, freshness, category, product, version and search.

The existing Integration Results page remains the operational run/finding view; this new page is the analytic inventory view.

### Implementation order

1. Add the optional SecMan contract and additive database migration.
2. Implement backend validation, lifecycle, REST/MCP reads and tests.
3. Add extension models, deterministic detection, reports and MariaDB migration.
4. Add `--targets-from-secman` with direct subject identity.
5. Add the analytics UI.
6. Update central and extension documentation and integration fixtures.
7. Run extension verification, focused root tests, integration-contract checks, OWASP review, then mandated E2E gates in a confirmed disposable environment.

The two defaults I would carry into implementation are: MariaDB remains the local database, and REST is canonical while SOAP stays out unless you identify a concrete SOAP consumer and contract.

Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is enabled.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.

---
name: secure-code
description: >

  writing** any backend endpoint, repository query, MCP tool, file upload,
  export, HTML sink or outbound HTTP call, and whenever the user says "secure
  code", "write this securely", "generate secure code", "owasp", "security
  check", "is this secure", "harden this", "security review before I commit",
  or asks for code in a security-sensitive area. Not a substitute for
  `/security-review` — it invokes it.
---

> **Sync policy (two-way, mandatory)**: This file and
> `.claude/skills/secure-code/SKILL.md` are one skill kept in two harness trees
> — Codex reads this copy, Claude Code reads the other. Whichever copy an
> agent edits, the same change is ported to the other **in the same commit**;
> translate harness-specific mechanics rather than copying verbatim (e.g.
> `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"` ↔ Bash tool
> `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`). `.claude/skills/` is the tie-breaker
> when the two disagree — that is a conflict rule, not a licence to edit one

> calling the change done. See `CLAUDE.md` §"Tooling Conventions" and
> `AGENTS.md` §Skills.

# Secure code generation — OWASP Top 10:2021 by construction

This skill is for the agent **doing the writing**, and it is deliberately not
delegated to a separate reviewer that runs afterwards. Its job is to shape code
before it exists; handing it to something downstream would put the guidance
where the writing is not happening.

## The problem this solves

`CLAUDE.md` §"OWASP Top 10 Compliance" is already binding policy, and it is
already good. It is also ~60 bullet points spanning ten categories, which is
more than anyone holds in working memory while writing a controller. The
predictable failure is not defiance, it is **partial recall**: you remember
`@Secured` and forget that the id in the path is untrusted; you remember to
bind `:name` and forget `ExcelSanitizer` on the export three files over.

So this skill does three things policy prose cannot:

1. **Narrows ten categories to the three that your change can actually
   violate**, before you write anything.
2. **Names the one existing function to call** for each — because the second
   implementation of a control is how the first one gets bypassed.
3. **Verifies mechanically**, so "I followed the rules" becomes a red or green
   exit code instead of a claim.

Security-first is Hard Principle 1 and the OWASP checklist is binding, not
advisory. This skill is how that gets operationalized; it does not add new
policy, and where this file and `CLAUDE.md` ever disagree, `CLAUDE.md` wins.

---

## Phase 1 — Route the change (before writing code)

Answer these about what you are about to build. Every **yes** pulls in a row.
Do not read all ten categories; read the rows you matched, then their entries
in `references/controls.md`.

| If the change… | Categories | The control you must reuse |
|---|---|---|
| adds or edits an HTTP endpoint | A01, A04 | `@Secured` + narrowest role; deny by default |
| accepts an **id** from the client | **A01** | `AssetFilterService.canAccessAsset` / `getAccessibleAssetIds` |
| adds or edits an MCP tool | **A01** | `McpToolPermissions.LISTING` **and** `.CALLING` + an `McpToolGuards` check |
| writes a query (JPQL, native, criteria) | A03, A01 | bound `:params`; allowlist enum for column/sort/table |
| returns a list | A04 | page at the query — never `findAll()` then slice |
| renders user-supplied HTML | A03 | `DOMPurify.sanitize` **at the assignment site** |
| writes an Excel/CSV cell | A03 | `ExcelSanitizer.sanitize` on every user-controlled cell |
| accepts a file upload | A08 | `ImportController.validateFile` shape: size, extension, content type, non-empty — **before parsing** |
| parses XML | A08 | the four `setFeature` calls from `NmapParserService` |
| reads an archive | A08 | reject `..` entries, bound the decompressed size |
| makes an outbound HTTP call | **A10** | `https` + host allowlist; reject loopback/link-local/RFC-1918/`169.254.169.254`; never follow redirects out of policy |
| touches passwords, keys or tokens | A02, A07 | `BCryptPasswordEncoder`; JWT stays in the HttpOnly `secman_auth` cookie |
| stores a credential | A02 | `EncryptedStringConverter`, never returned, `***HIDDEN***` means "keep" |
| adds config, CORS or headers | A05 | explicit origin allowlist; never weaken `SecurityHeadersFilter` |
| adds a dependency | A06 | prefer the classpath; pin exact; `src/clinotify` is stdlib-only |
| logs anything | A09 | actor + target + outcome; never the secret's **value**; strip CR/LF |
| catches an exception | A09 | never an empty block |
| returns an error to a client | A05 | generic message out, detail to the server log |

**Say out loud which rows you matched.** A change that matches no row is
almost always a change you have not finished describing to yourself.

## Phase 2 — Write it with the existing control

Read `references/controls.md` for the matched rows: it holds the canonical
snippet and the file that already does it correctly, so the new code can copy a
control that is already reviewed rather than invent a parallel one.

Three rules govern the writing itself:

- **Reuse, never re-implement.** If a control exists, call it. A second
  sanitizer, second URL validator, second permission check is a divergence that
  will be patched on one side only.
- **Never work around a control to make something build, start or pass.**
  `JwtSigningValidator`, `DatabaseCredentialValidator` and
  `DatasourceUrlValidator` fail the boot on weak config *by design*. A test that
  needs `HttpOnly: false`, a feature that needs `unsafe-eval`, an import that
  needs the XXE block relaxed — change the test, the feature, the import.
- **Deny by default.** Start from the narrowest role that works and widen
  deliberately. `IS_AUTHENTICATED` with a TODO is not a decision.

## Phase 3 — Verify

Three checks, in this order. None replaces another: the first is mechanical and
blind, the second is semantic and unautomatable, the third is adversarial.

### 3a. Static gate (always)

```bash
./scripts/owasp-check.sh            # this change vs origin/main, includes untracked files
./scripts/owasp-check.sh --verbose  # same, with the offending line text
```

Findings come in two severities:

- **BLOCK** — introduced by *this* change. Fix it. Exit code 1. A BLOCK finding
  means the change is not complete, in the same sense a failing build is not
  complete.
- **REVIEW** — a pattern worth a decision, often pre-existing in a file you
  touched. Look at each one and **state what you decided**. "Reviewed, the id
  is workgroup-scoped by the caller" is an answer; silence is not.

Two things it will not do, by design: it does not scan the whole repo unless
asked (`--all`, for audits — the repo has substantial pre-existing findings and
a gate that is red on arrival is a gate people learn to ignore), and it does not
edit anything.

If you believe a BLOCK finding is a false positive, do not silence it locally —
say so explicitly in your report and, if the pattern is genuinely approved,
tighten the rule in `scripts/owasp-check.sh` **and** add the approved pattern to
`scripts/test/owasp-check-test.sh` as an `expect_silent` case, so the exemption
is tested rather than remembered.

### 3b. Semantic re-read (always)

The scanner sees text. Roughly half of the OWASP rules here are about meaning
and no grep will ever catch them. Read `references/blind-spots.md` and walk your
diff against it — that file is the checklist for exactly the failures a green
scanner cannot rule out, chiefly:

- Is that id **actually** owner-scoped, or does the query just happen to filter?
- Is the role the **narrowest** one that works, or the first one that compiled?
- Is the business invariant enforced **server-side**, or only in the UI?
- Does the error message distinguish "no such account" from "wrong password"?
- Is the new outbound host reachable at an internal address?

### 3c. `/security-review` (conditionally, and it blocks)

Run it on the branch diff when the change touches **authentication,
authorization, crypto, file upload, export, or any outbound HTTP call** —
`CLAUDE.md`'s review gate requires this, and `/finalizer` runs a HIGH/CRITICAL
pass at the end anyway.

**A finding at HIGH or above blocks the change.** Fix it. Noting it is not
closing it.

### 3d. Report the verdict

Close with the single line `CLAUDE.md`'s review gate asks for, naming only the
categories the change actually touched:

```
OWASP: A01/A03/A09 touched — clean
```

If something is unresolved, say so in the same line rather than omitting it:

```
OWASP: A01/A10 touched — A10 outbound host allowlist deferred, see note below
```

---

## What this skill is not

- **Not a replacement for `/security-review`** — step 3c invokes it.
